## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.

- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-828` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +651
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:27:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T06:27:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

## Machine jobs

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T06:27:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

Also, in `action()`, for a PR in state OPEN, `pr = prRef && prRef.state === 'OPEN' ? provider.prStatus(prRef.number) : prRef`. So pr.headSha comes from computePrStatus — it does set headSha (line 377). Good.

2. **Gate on the verdict record: verdictRecords without author allowlist** — pre-existing (gh-807 shipped without the allowlist in both readers). Note in general comment.

3. **`selectResolvableThreads` uses `effective.record.verdict !== 'APPROVE'`** — good. But one subtle issue: the gate checks `blocking == 0` census. But the record's census also could have `suggestions > 0` — not required. OK.

4. **Potential issue: `threadSeverity` body check is on the ROOT comment only.** The severity marker lives in the machine's inline comment files, which are posted as review thread bodies. Actually, machine review threads: each inline comment body contains e.g. "💡 **SUGGESTION**" or the content of the comment file. The root comment of the thread is the machine's comment. Fine.

5. **BLOCKING marker false-positive risk**: `SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — word "blocking" anywhere in the body, case-insensitive, e.g. "non-blocking" contains "blocking" as part of hyphenated word. `\b` before B: in "non-blocking", there's a word boundary at "blocking" (after hyphen)? Hyphen is a non-word character, so `non-blocking` — between `n` and `-` there's a boundary, and between `-` and `b` there's a boundary. So `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking"! Hmm. Does any machine comment say "non-blocking"? The ack reply itself says "non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict (gh-828)". If the machine re-evaluates a thread whose ack was already posted (but the resolve failed), the body now contains "non-blocking"... wait, the ack is a REPLY to the thread, not the root. reviewThreadList takes `comments.nodes[0]` — the root comment. Ack replies are appended later, so root body stays the original. OK. But could a machine review thread's root body legitimately contain "blocking" while being non-blocking? E.g. a suggestion comment saying "this is not blocking, but..." — the review comment bodies are markdown files. A 💡 SUGGESTION comment could plausibly contain the word "blocking" ("not a blocking issue"). That would misclassify as blocking → thread never resolves → PR stays BLOCKED forever → the very stall this PR fixes. But it's fail-safe direction (won't wrongly resolve), just potentially strands. Given the census gate is the authority and the marker is a cross-check, this is a SUGGESTION-level concern about the regex matching hyphenated "blocking". Actually also "unblocking" — `\b` prevents prefix matches for word chars, but hyphen is fine. Worth a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Since these threads are machine-authored with a strict marker convention (🚨 BLOCKING / ⚠️ IMPORTANT / 💡 SUGGESTION), the marker is usually at the start. A safer classification would prioritize the first line or require the marker emoji. I'll flag as SUGGESTION.

6. **Skip-count semantics in `selectResolvableThreads`**: the loop `break`s when `resolvable.length >= max` — meaning skipped counts stop accumulating beyond cap; fine.

7. **`resolveSuggestionThreads` in machineSmAgent passes `cfg.maxResolveThreads`** — set in action(). Note `cfg.maxResolveThreads` computed only from `p.maxResolveThreads` (jobParams), not from `override` (project config). Minor inconsistency: other knobs honor `override` (projectConfig.machineSm) first. `machineLogins` uses resolveMachineAuthor(p, projectConfig) — honors project config. But `maxResolveThreads` ignores `override.maxResolveThreads`. SUGGESTION.

8. **ack reply failure still resolves thread**: if replyToThread throws but resolveThread succeeds, the thread is resolved without the ack. Acceptable per "never abort", noted.

9. **`reviewThreadList` GraphQL pagination**: reviewThreads.nodes without pageInfo — for ≤20 threads fine, first page only. If a PR has >100 threads? Edge case; cap 20. Fine but the fail-open means if first page lacks the unresolved ones... threads are typically returned in order; low risk. SUGGESTION at most.

10. **BLOCKED also on pending required checks**: the code acknowledges it's a harmless no-op. But wait — one subtle thing: `pr.checkConclusion === 'pending'` returns skip earlier, so BLOCKED branch only on green. Good.

11. **mergeable parity**: `pr.mergeState === 'CLEAN' || pr.mergeable === true` — merge happens first; BLOCKED branch comes after CLEAN check. What if mergeState is BLOCKED but mergeable is true? Then merge action fires (the CLEAN/mergeable check comes first). OK.

12. **dryRun**: executeAction not called in dry run. Good.

13. **headSha on action**: `a.headSha = (pr && pr.headSha) || null` — pr is null when findPr returns null, but then decideActions would dispatch/skip without resolveSuggestionThreads (no pr). OK. But if `prRef.state === 'OPEN'`, `pr = provider.prStatus(prRef.number)` which could return... computePrStatus always includes headSha. Good.

14. **AC1 wording "one ack comment"**: PR resolves as one ack per thread — documented in PR description. Fine.

15. **Missing author allowlist on verdictRecords (forge hardening)**: the module doc (gh-807 round 3) explicitly says "The READERS always pass an allowlist (an empty one trusts nothing)". Both readers (smProvider.verdictRecords and smAgent.readVerdictRecords) don't. This is pre-existing unchanged code, but this PR builds a new security-relevant consumer on it: with a forged APPROVE marker (marker format is public — stated in the doc), an attacker/any commenter could make the tick resolve machine threads on a head whose real verdict was REQUEST_CHANGES. Impact limited (resolving machine's own non-blocking threads), but it defeats AC2's spirit. IMPORTANT, but the line to attach: the diff doesn't touch verdictRecords. Per rules, findings on unchanged code go in the general comment. Actually the new consumer line IS in the diff: machineSmAgent.js line 260 `var records = provider.verdictRecords(prNumber);`. I could attach the inline comment there since that line is in the diff. Yes — line 260 is added in the diff.

16. **`threadSeverity` classification order**: blocking checked before important before suggestion — a body containing both 🚨 and 💡 (e.g. a summary comment) → blocking. Conservative, fine.

17. **`machineLogins` empty → fail closed**: yes.

18. **Comments pagination**: verdictRecords reads github_get_pr_comments; existing behavior.

19. **`console.warn` emoji in GraalJS pack**: fine.

20. **test_smProvider loadProvider**: uses rvReal? Let me look at test_smProvider new suite — it loads reviewVerdicts real via makeRequire({'./reviewVerdicts.js': rvReal()}). Wait in the diff snippet: `makeRequire({ './reviewVerdicts.js': rvReal() }, mocks || {})` — but `rvReal` is defined where? The diff shows `function loadProvider(mocks) { var mod = loadModule(MOD, makeRequire({ './reviewVerdicts.js': rvReal() }, mocks || {}), mocks || {}); ...` and I don't see rvReal defined in the new suite. Let me check the full test file — rvReal may be defined in an earlier suite (gh-807 suite). Let me check.

Also check whether smProvider's githubProvider actually requires reviewVerdicts at top (it references `reviewVerdicts.parseVerdictRecords` in verdictRecords — pre-existing from gh-807).

Let me check test_smProvider for rvReal definition.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.
