So pr.headSha comes from computePrStatus — it does set headSha (line 377). Good.

2. **Gate on the verdict record: verdictRecords without author allowlist** — pre-existing (gh-807 shipped without the allowlist in both readers). Note in general comment.

3. **`selectResolvableThreads` uses `effective.record.verdict !== 'APPROVE'`** — good. But one subtle issue: the gate checks `blocking == 0` census. But the record's census also could have `suggestions > 0` — not required. OK.

4. **Potential issue: `threadSeverity` body check is on the ROOT comment only.** The severity marker lives in the machine's inline comment files, which are posted as review thread bodies. Actually, machine review threads: each inline comment body contains e.g. "💡 **SUGGESTION**" or the content of the comment file. The root comment of the thread is the machine's comment. Fine.

5. **BLOCKING marker false-positive risk**: `SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — word "blocking" anywhere in the body, case-insensitive, e.g. "non-blocking" contains "blocking" as part of hyphenated word. `\b` before B: in "non-blocking", there's a word boundary at "blocking" (after hyphen)? Hyphen is a non-word character, so `non-blocking` — between `n` and `-` there's a boundary, and between `-` and `b` there's a boundary. So `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking"! Hmm. Does any machine comment say "non-blocking"? The ack reply itself says "non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict (gh-828)". If the machine re-evaluates a thread whose ack was already posted (but the resolve failed), the body now contains "non-blocking"... wait, the ack is a REPLY to the thread, not the root. reviewThreadList takes `comments.nodes[0]` — the root comment. Ack replies are appended later, so root body stays the original. OK. But could a machine review thread's root body legitimately contain "blocking" while being non-blocking? E.g. a suggestion comment saying "this is not blocking, but..." — the review comment bodies are markdown files. A 💡 SUGGESTION comment could plausibly contain the word "blocking" ("not a blocking issue"). That would misclassify as blocking → thread never resolves → PR stays BLOCKED forever → the very stall this PR fixes. But it's fail-safe direction (won't wrongly resolve), just potentially strands. Given the census gate is the authority and the marker is a cross-check, this is a SUGGESTION-level concern about the regex matching hyphenated "blocking". Actually also "unblocking" — `\b` prevents prefix matches for word chars, but hyphen is fine. Worth a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Since these threads are machine-authored with a strict marker convention (🚨 BLOCKING / ⚠️ IMPORTANT / 💡 SUGGESTION), the marker is usually at the start. A safer classification would prioritize the first line or require the marker emoji. I'll flag as SUGGESTION.

Minor inconsistency: other knobs honor `override` (projectConfig.machineSm) first. `machineLogins` uses resolveMachineAuthor(p, projectConfig) — honors project config. But `maxResolveThreads` ignores `override.maxResolveThreads`. SUGGESTION.

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.

But BLOCKED due to a failing required check? checkConclusion would be 'red' → rework arm. So the resolveSuggestionThreads branch only fires on green + BLOCKED, which is the conversation gate (or non-check protections). Good.

One more consideration — the ordering issue in the mergeState determination: when base is fresh and REST reports BLOCKED, the conversation gate vs pending checks — checks are green here. OK.

Another check: `selectResolvableThreads` gate: what about `effective.record.verdict` case sensitivity? Records parsed via extractVerdictRecord are uppercased. But the machineSmAgent test RECORD uses 'APPROVE'. But `resolveSuggestionThreads` receives records from `provider.verdictRecords(prNumber)` which parses via parseVerdictRecords → uppercased. OK.

Now potential finding: `threadSeverity` on the ack reply - no.

Another potential issue: In `selectResolvableThreads`, `effective.record.verdict !== 'APPROVE'` — but records built via parseVerdictRecords are uppercased. OK.

Now the severity regex `\bBLOCKING\b` matching "non-blocking" — actually wait, let me verify: `/\bBLOCKING\b/i.test('non-blocking')`. Hyphen: "non-blocking" — positions: n-o-n-`-b... `\b` is between a word char and non-word char. `-` is non-word, `b` is word → boundary exists. And end "g" word char followed by end → boundary. So yes, it matches. A machine suggestion comment containing "non-blocking" (e.g. "this is non-blocking, but consider...") would be classified 'blocking' → never auto-resolved → PR stranded BLOCKED → exactly the failure mode this PR fixes, but now permanent for that thread. It keeps the rework arm? No — armReworkDecision withholds the rework arm for APPROVE regardless of open threads (blocking=0 census, suggestions>0 arms rework... wait: armReworkDecision arms rework when suggestions > 0! "an APPROVE record reporting blocking > 0 — or suggestions > 0 — is the evidence AC3's census exceptions arm on". So with suggestions>0, the rework arm CAN be armed, and the rework leg owns thread resolution, so it would resolve eventually. Hmm — but gh-807's withheld-arm... The PR description says "gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → 'suggestions do not trigger rework')". There's a contradiction between reviewVerdicts armReworkDecision (arms on suggestions>0) and the PR description... but that's gh-807 territory; non-goal here.

So misclassification direction: fail-closed (won't resolve). Combined with suggestions>0 arming rework, probably self-healing. SUGGESTION severity.

Now the more significant finding — severity of "verdictRecords without author allowlist". The reviewVerdicts module doc explicitly documents the forge hardening requirement (gh-807 review round 3): "The READERS always pass an allowlist... A marker posted by ANY other identity is invisible — the marker format is public (this repo), so an unauthenticated APPROVE could otherwise withhold rework arms, unblock pr_approved-gated lanes or strip legitimate arms." The readers in fact do NOT pass it (pre-existing). This PR adds a new consumer whose gate (APPROVE + blocking=0) authorizes the machine to resolve its own review threads — a forged APPROVE marker on a head with a real REQUEST_CHANGES verdict would cause the machine to resolve all its non-blocking threads and clear the conversation gate, enabling merge of unaddressed review findings? Wait — merge requires pr_approved label. A forged record doesn't add the label. The new consumer only resolves threads; the merge leg requires pr_approved + green + CLEAN. So the forge's blast radius: machine threads get resolved prematurely, defeating AC2. The rework arm decision (armReworkDecision) uses records too — same forge could suppress rework. All pre-existing. But per instructions: "Flag deviations from established patterns" and findings on unchanged code go in general comment. I think this deserves an IMPORTANT inline comment attached to the new consumer line (js/machineSmAgent.js:260 — added line in the diff), noting the new leg inherits the missing allowlist and the fix is to pass the machine-author allowlist through verdictRecords.

Actually, is it really exploitable? To post a comment on the PR you need write access (triage/comment). An insider with comment access could forge. The gh-807 doc considered this threat model. I'll classify IMPORTANT.

Now check one more thing: does the `replyToThread` fallback for missing rootCommentId post a PR-level comment — that could spam the PR with one ack comment per thread lacking a root comment id. But reviewThreadList always sets rootCommentId from first.databaseId — for GitHub GraphQL, databaseId exists. The fallback path: thread selected only if threadId exists; rootCommentId may be null if databaseId missing → PR-level comment per thread → comment spam (up to 20/tick). Edge case; also each such comment is a new PR comment which is itself a "thread"? No, plain comments don't block the conversation gate. SUGGESTION at most. Also note: those PR-level ack comments are authored by machine — the verdictRecords parser reads PR comments — ack contains no marker. OK.

Also: `body: first.body` — the ack replies posted into threads are included in comments.nodes but only [0] is read. Fine.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 831
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/831
- **Title**: gh-828 [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-828` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +651
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:27:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T06:27:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

But wait: there's a subtlety — checkConclusion 'pending' is checked BEFORE the pr_approved branch, so BLOCKED+pends → skip. But BLOCKED due to a failing required check? checkConclusion would be 'red' → rework arm. So the resolveSuggestionThreads branch only fires on green + BLOCKED, which is the conversation gate (or non-check protections). Good.

One more consideration — the ordering issue in the mergeState determination: when base is fresh and REST reports BLOCKED, the conversation gate vs pending checks — checks are green here. OK.

Another check: `selectResolvableThreads` gate: what about `effective.record.verdict` case sensitivity? Records parsed via extractVerdictRecord are uppercased. But the machineSmAgent test RECORD uses 'APPROVE'. But `resolveSuggestionThreads` receives records from `provider.verdictRecords(prNumber)` which parses via parseVerdictRecords → uppercased. OK.

Now potential finding: `threadSeverity` on the ack reply - no.

Another potential issue: In `selectResolvableThreads`, `effective.record.verdict !== 'APPROVE'` — but records built via parseVerdictRecords are uppercased. OK.

Now the severity regex `\bBLOCKING\b` matching "non-blocking" — actually wait, let me verify: `/\bBLOCKING\b/i.test('non-blocking')`. Hyphen: "non-blocking" — positions: n-o-n-`-b... `\b` is between a word char and non-word char. `-` is non-word, `b` is word → boundary exists. And end "g" word char followed by end → boundary. So yes, it matches. A machine suggestion comment containing "non-blocking" (e.g. "this is non-blocking, but consider...") would be classified 'blocking' → never auto-resolved → PR stranded BLOCKED → exactly the failure mode this PR fixes, but now permanent for that thread. It keeps the rework arm? No — armReworkDecision withholds the rework arm for APPROVE regardless of open threads (blocking=0 census, suggestions>0 arms rework... wait: armReworkDecision arms rework when suggestions > 0! "an APPROVE record reporting blocking > 0 — or suggestions > 0 — is the evidence AC3's census exceptions arm on". So with suggestions>0, the rework arm CAN be armed, and the rework leg owns thread resolution, so it would resolve eventually. Hmm — but gh-807's withheld-arm... The PR description says "gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → 'suggestions do not trigger rework')". There's a contradiction between reviewVerdicts armReworkDecision (arms on suggestions>0) and the PR description... but that's gh-807 territory; non-goal here.

So misclassification direction: fail-closed (won't resolve). Combined with suggestions>0 arming rework, probably self-healing. SUGGESTION severity.

Now the more significant finding — severity of "verdictRecords without author allowlist". The reviewVerdicts module doc explicitly documents the forge hardening requirement (gh-807 review round 3): "The READERS always pass an allowlist... A marker posted by ANY other identity is invisible — the marker format is public (this repo), so an unauthenticated APPROVE could otherwise withhold rework arms, unblock pr_approved-gated lanes or strip legitimate arms." The readers in fact do NOT pass it (pre-existing). re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

While that runs, continue the review. Key areas to scrutinize:

1. **`decideActions` — BLOCKED branch reachability**: `pr.mergeState === 'BLOCKED'` — is BLOCKED actually the value reported by computePrStatus? Let me check computePrStatus's mergeState values. Also, in `action()`, for a PR in state OPEN, `pr = prRef && prRef.state === 'OPEN' ? provider.prStatus(prRef.number) : prRef`. So pr.headSha comes from computePrStatus — it does set headSha (line 377). Good.

2. **Gate on the verdict record: verdictRecords without author allowlist** — pre-existing (gh-807 shipped without the allowlist in both readers). Note in general comment.

3. **`selectResolvableThreads` uses `effective.record.verdict !== 'APPROVE'`** — good. But one subtle issue: the gate checks `blocking == 0` census. But the record's census also could have `suggestions > 0` — not required. OK.

4. **Potential issue: `threadSeverity` body check is on the ROOT comment only.** The severity marker lives in the machine's inline comment files, which are posted as review thread bodies. Actually, machine review threads: each inline comment body contains e.g. "💡 **SUGGESTION**" or the content of the comment file. The root comment of the thread is the machine's comment. Fine.

5. **BLOCKING marker false-positive risk**: `SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — word "blocking" anywhere in the body, case-insensitive, e.g. "non-blocking" contains "blocking" as part of hyphenated word. `\b` before B: in "non-blocking", there's a word boundary at "blocking" (after hyphen)? Hyphen is a non-word character, so `non-blocking` — between `n` and `-` there's a boundary, and between `-` and `b` there's a boundary. So `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking"! Hmm. Does any machine comment say "non-blocking"? The ack reply itself says "non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict (gh-828)". If the machine re-evaluates a thread whose ack was already posted (but the resolve failed), the body now contains "non-blocking"... wait, the ack is a REPLY to the thread, not the root. reviewThreadList takes `comments.nodes[0]` — the root comment. Ack replies are appended later, so root body stays the original. OK. But could a machine review thread's root body legitimately contain "blocking" while being non-blocking? E.g. a suggestion comment saying "this is not blocking, but..." — the review comment bodies are markdown files. A 💡 SUGGESTION comment could plausibly contain the word "blocking" ("not a blocking issue"). That would misclassify as blocking → thread never resolves → PR stays BLOCKED forever → the very stall this PR fixes. But it's fail-safe direction (won't wrongly resolve), just potentially strands. Given the census gate is the authority and the marker is a cross-check, this is a SUGGESTION-level concern about the regex matching hyphenated "blocking". Actually also "unblocking" — `\b` prevents prefix matches for word chars, but hyphen is fine. Worth a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? Since these threads are machine-authored with a strict marker convention (🚨 BLOCKING / ⚠️ IMPORTANT / 💡 SUGGESTION), the marker is usually at the start. ## PR Description

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

# PR Review — gh-828 (#831)

## Summary

Solid, well-tested fix for the real 8h BLOCKED fleet stall: pure selection helpers with fail-closed gates, provider primitives with fail-open reads, per-thread failure isolation, and genuinely good test coverage (AC1 replay, AC2/AC3, fail-closed paths, idempotency, gitlab no-op). Verified locally: `run_all.json` → **2299 passed, 0 failed**; new `run_machineSmAgent.json` → 29 passed. Ticket ACs 1–3 are covered by unit tests; AC4 is live-verification as designed.

## Key Issues

- ⚠️ **`threadSeverity` word-regex matches "non-blocking"** — `\bBLOCKING\b` matches the tail of "non-blocking"/"unblocking", so a machine suggestion comment containing that phrase is classified `blocking`, never auto-resolved, and can re-strand the PR BLOCKED (reviewVerdicts.js:380).
- ⚠️ **The new gate trusts unauthenticated verdict records** — `provider.verdictRecords(prNumber)` parses markers without the machine-author allowlist the module itself mandates, so a marker forged by any comment-capable identity defeats AC2 (machineSmAgent.js:260). Pre-existing reader gap, but this PR's gate is its highest-stakes consumer.
- 💡 Ack reply is not idempotent: if `resolveThread` fails after the ack posted, the next tick posts another ack to the same thread (machineSmAgent.js:279).
- 💡 `maxResolveThreads` ignores the project-config `machineSm` override priority every other knob honors (machineSmAgent.js:325).

## Next Steps

1. Fix the severity regex (emoji-first, or a `(?:^|[^\w-])` guard before the word `BLOCKING`).
2. Thread the gh-728 machine-author allowlist into `verdictRecords` / `readVerdictRecords` (or document the accepted forge risk explicitly).
3. Optional: swap resolve-then-reply or dedupe acks on re-tick; honor `override.maxResolveThreads`.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking" — suggestion threads can be misclassified and re-strand the PR**

`SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — the `\b` boundary holds across a hyphen, so any machine comment containing "non-blocking" / "unblocking" (very plausible in a reviewer's own suggestion prose, e.g. *"this is non-blocking, but consider renaming"*) classifies as `blocking`. Consequences:

- The thread is excluded from auto-resolution and keeps the rework arm — fine in isolation.
- But on an APPROVE + `blocking=0` head the rework arm is withheld (gh-828's own premise), so this thread is now owned by **nobody**: the new leg skips it, the rework arm never fires, and the conversation gate holds the PR BLOCKED — a permanent, per-thread recurrence of the exact 8h stall this PR fixes. Verified: `/\bBLOCKING\b/i.test('this is non-blocking, but consider renaming')` → `true`.

Fail-closed direction is right (a misclassified thread is never *wrongly resolved*), so this is not a merge blocker — but the classifier should match the marker convention precisely. Suggested fix: check the emoji markers first and require the word form to not follow a hyphen/word char:

```javascript
var SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|((?:^|[^\w-])BLOCKING\b)/i;
```

A test with body `'💡 SUGGESTION: this is non-blocking, but rename'` → `'suggestion'` would pin it.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the ack reply is not idempotent — a persistent resolve failure spams one ack per tick**

The selection filters *resolved* threads, but the ack reply is posted **before** the resolve. If `replyToThread` succeeds and `resolveThread` throws (transient GraphQL error, token permission drift), the thread stays unresolved; next tick it is selected again and another ack is posted — one duplicate ack per tick per thread, unbounded, until the resolve starts succeeding (or forever, if the failure is persistent and the reply keeps working).

Cheapest fix: resolve first, then reply only when the resolve succeeded (a resolved thread missing its ack is a cosmetic loss; the code already tolerates `replyToThread` failing after a successful resolve — the information value of the ack is identical either way). Alternatively keep the order but track per-thread "ack already posted" — though no cross-tick state exists today.

Not blocking: requires resolve to keep failing while reply keeps succeeding, and the PR-level fallback path in `replyToThread` makes duplicate acks visible rather than destructive.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `maxResolveThreads` bypasses the documented override priority**

Every other `machineSm` knob resolves `override` (`.dmtools/config.js` `machineSm` section) before `p` (jobParams): `dryRun`, `maxConcurrentRuns`, `maxReworkRounds`, `workflowFile`, `issueLimit`… `maxResolveThreads` reads only `p.maxResolveThreads`, so a project that configures `machineSm: { maxResolveThreads: 5 }` in `.dmtools/config.js` gets the default 20 with no warning — surprising for an operator tuning the exact API-call bound this knob exists to control. One-liner for parity:

```javascript
cfg.maxResolveThreads = (typeof override.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && override.maxResolveThreads > 0)
    ? Math.floor(override.maxResolveThreads)
    : (typeof p.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && p.maxResolveThreads > 0)
        ? Math.floor(p.maxResolveThreads) : reviewVerdictsModule.DEFAULT_RESOLVE_THREADS_CAP;
```

Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

## Summary

Solid, well-tested fix for the real 8h BLOCKED fleet stall: pure selection helpers with fail-closed gates, provider primitives with fail-open reads, per-thread failure isolation, and genuinely good test coverage (AC1 replay, AC2/AC3, fail-closed paths, idempotency, gitlab no-op). - 💡 Ack reply is not idempotent: if `resolveThread` fails after the ack posted, the next tick posts another ack to the same thread (machineSmAgent.js:279).
- 💡 `maxResolveThreads` ignores the project-config `machineSm` override priority every other knob honors (machineSmAgent.js:325).

2. Thread the gh-728 machine-author allowlist into `verdictRecords` / `readVerdictRecords` (or document the accepted forge risk explicitly).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking" — suggestion threads can be misclassified and re-strand the PR**

`SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — the `\b` boundary holds across a hyphen, so any machine comment containing "non-blocking" / "unblocking" (very plausible in a reviewer's own suggestion prose, e.g. *"this is non-blocking, but consider renaming"*) classifies as `blocking`. Consequences:

- The thread is excluded from auto-resolution and keeps the rework arm — fine in isolation.
- But on an APPROVE + `blocking=0` head the rework arm is withheld (gh-828's own premise), so this thread is now owned by **nobody**: the new leg skips it, the rework arm never fires, and the conversation gate holds the PR BLOCKED — a permanent, per-thread recurrence of the exact 8h stall this PR fixes. Verified: `/\bBLOCKING\b/i.test('this is non-blocking, but consider renaming')` → `true`.

Fail-closed direction is right (a misclassified thread is never *wrongly resolved*), so this is not a merge blocker — but the classifier should match the marker convention precisely. Suggested fix: check the emoji markers first and require the word form to not follow a hyphen/word char:

```javascript
var SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|((?:^|[^\w-])BLOCKING\b)/i;
```

A test with body `'💡 SUGGESTION: this is non-blocking, but rename'` → `'suggestion'` would pin it.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the ack reply is not idempotent — a persistent resolve failure spams one ack per tick**

The selection filters *resolved* threads, but the ack reply is posted **before** the resolve. If `replyToThread` succeeds and `resolveThread` throws (transient GraphQL error, token permission drift), the thread stays unresolved; next tick it is selected again and another ack is posted — one duplicate ack per tick per thread, unbounded, until the resolve starts succeeding (or forever, if the failure is persistent and the reply keeps working).

Cheapest fix: resolve first, then reply only when the resolve succeeded (a resolved thread missing its ack is a cosmetic loss; the code already tolerates `replyToThread` failing after a successful resolve — the information value of the ack is identical either way). Alternatively keep the order but track per-thread "ack already posted" — though no cross-tick state exists today.

Not blocking: requires resolve to keep failing while reply keeps succeeding, and the PR-level fallback path in `replyToThread` makes duplicate acks visible rather than destructive.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `maxResolveThreads` bypasses the documented override priority**

Every other `machineSm` knob resolves `override` (`.dmtools/config.js` `machineSm` section) before `p` (jobParams): `dryRun`, `maxConcurrentRuns`, `maxReworkRounds`, `workflowFile`, `issueLimit`… `maxResolveThreads` reads only `p.maxResolveThreads`, so a project that configures `machineSm: { maxResolveThreads: 5 }` in `.dmtools/config.js` gets the default 20 with no warning — surprising for an operator tuning the exact API-call bound this knob exists to control. One-liner for parity:

```javascript
cfg.maxResolveThreads = (typeof override.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && override.maxResolveThreads > 0)
    ? Math.floor(override.maxResolveThreads)
    : (typeof p.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && p.maxResolveThreads > 0)
        ? Math.floor(p.maxResolveThreads) : reviewVerdictsModule.DEFAULT_RESOLVE_THREADS_CAP;
```

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## Summary

Solid, well-tested fix for the real 8h BLOCKED fleet stall: pure selection helpers with fail-closed gates, provider primitives with fail-open reads, per-thread failure isolation, and genuinely good test coverage (AC1 replay, AC2/AC3, fail-closed paths, idempotency, gitlab no-op). ## Key Issues

- ⚠️ **`threadSeverity` word-regex matches "non-blocking"** — `\bBLOCKING\b` matches the tail of "non-blocking"/"unblocking", so a machine suggestion comment containing that phrase is classified `blocking`, never auto-resolved, and can re-strand the PR BLOCKED (reviewVerdicts.js:380).

Pre-existing reader gap, but this PR's gate is its highest-stakes consumer.
- 💡 Ack reply is not idempotent: if `resolveThread` fails after the ack posted, the next tick posts another ack to the same thread (machineSmAgent.js:279).
- 💡 `maxResolveThreads` ignores the project-config `machineSm` override priority every other knob honors (machineSmAgent.js:325).

## Next Steps

1. Fix the severity regex (emoji-first, or a `(?:^|[^\w-])` guard before the word `BLOCKING`).
2. Thread the gh-728 machine-author allowlist into `verdictRecords` / `readVerdictRecords` (or document the accepted forge risk explicitly).
3. Optional: swap resolve-then-reply or dedupe acks on re-tick; honor `override.maxResolveThreads`.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking" — suggestion threads can be misclassified and re-strand the PR**

`SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — the `\b` boundary holds across a hyphen, so any machine comment containing "non-blocking" / "unblocking" (very plausible in a reviewer's own suggestion prose, e.g. *"this is non-blocking, but consider renaming"*) classifies as `blocking`. Consequences:

- The thread is excluded from auto-resolution and keeps the rework arm — fine in isolation.
- But on an APPROVE + `blocking=0` head the rework arm is withheld (gh-828's own premise), so this thread is now owned by **nobody**: the new leg skips it, the rework arm never fires, and the conversation gate holds the PR BLOCKED — a permanent, per-thread recurrence of the exact 8h stall this PR fixes. Verified: `/\bBLOCKING\b/i.test('this is non-blocking, but consider renaming')` → `true`.

Fail-closed direction is right (a misclassified thread is never *wrongly resolved*), so this is not a merge blocker — but the classifier should match the marker convention precisely. Suggested fix: check the emoji markers first and require the word form to not follow a hyphen/word char:

```javascript
var SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|((?:^|[^\w-])BLOCKING\b)/i;
```

A test with body `'💡 SUGGESTION: this is non-blocking, but rename'` → `'suggestion'` would pin it.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the ack reply is not idempotent — a persistent resolve failure spams one ack per tick**

The selection filters *resolved* threads, but the ack reply is posted **before** the resolve. If `replyToThread` succeeds and `resolveThread` throws (transient GraphQL error, token permission drift), the thread stays unresolved; next tick it is selected again and another ack is posted — one duplicate ack per tick per thread, unbounded, until the resolve starts succeeding (or forever, if the failure is persistent and the reply keeps working).

Cheapest fix: resolve first, then reply only when the resolve succeeded (a resolved thread missing its ack is a cosmetic loss; the code already tolerates `replyToThread` failing after a successful resolve — the information value of the ack is identical either way). Alternatively keep the order but track per-thread "ack already posted" — though no cross-tick state exists today.

Not blocking: requires resolve to keep failing while reply keeps succeeding, and the PR-level fallback path in `replyToThread` makes duplicate acks visible rather than destructive.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `maxResolveThreads` bypasses the documented override priority**

Every other `machineSm` knob resolves `override` (`.dmtools/config.js` `machineSm` section) before `p` (jobParams): `dryRun`, `maxConcurrentRuns`, `maxReworkRounds`, `workflowFile`, `issueLimit`… `maxResolveThreads` reads only `p.maxResolveThreads`, so a project that configures `machineSm: { maxResolveThreads: 5 }` in `.dmtools/config.js` gets the default 20 with no warning — surprising for an operator tuning the exact API-call bound this knob exists to control. One-liner for parity:

```javascript
cfg.maxResolveThreads = (typeof override.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && override.maxResolveThreads > 0)
    ? Math.floor(override.maxResolveThreads)
    : (typeof p.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && p.maxResolveThreads > 0)
        ? Math.floor(p.maxResolveThreads) : reviewVerdictsModule.DEFAULT_RESOLVE_THREADS_CAP;
```

Closes #828
### Root Cause
Approve-with-suggestions PRs (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE, census `blocking=0`) deadlocked on repos with the "require conversation resolution" gate: gh-807 correctly withholds the rework arm, and the rework leg was the only owner of `resolveThread` — so the machine's own suggestion threads held approved heads `BLOCKED` forever (live fa #1457–#1470, ~8h fleet stall). `machineSmAgent.decideActions` treated every non-CLEAN/BEHIND approved state as a bare skip.

### Fix
- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — new pure helpers: `threadSeverity` (per-thread marker classification 🚨/⚠️/💡), `selectResolvableThreads` (gate: effective record for the current head must be APPROVE with `blocking==0`, else fail closed; then select unresolved, machine-authored, non-blocking threads, bounded to 20/tick), `buildThreadAckReply`.
- `js/common/smProvider.js` — GitHub provider gains `reviewThreadList` (resolve id + root comment id + author + body, fail-open `[]`), `replyToThread`, `resolveThread`.
- `js/machineSmAgent.js` — the approved+`BLOCKED` branch now emits a `resolveSuggestionThreads` action: per selected thread post the ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and resolve it in-tick. Machine logins come from the `machineAuthor` knob (gh-728 list); unconfigured → fail closed. Human threads never resolve (AC3); blocking-marked threads keep the rework arm (AC2).

### Test Coverage
- `test_reviewVerdicts.js` — 12 new gh-828 tests: severity mapping, AC1 selection + idempotency, AC2 blocking exclusion + census gate, AC3 human exclusion, fail-closed gates, bound, ack wording.
- `test_machineSmAgent.js` — approved+BLOCKED routes to the new action (replaces the old skip); #1457–#1470 replay: 4 suggestion threads → 4 acks + 4 resolves; AC2/AC3, fail-closed, gitlab no-op, per-thread failure isolation.
- `test_smProvider.js` — thread-list mapping/fail-open, reply/resolve tool contracts.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2276 passed, 0 failed. Added `run_machineSmAgent.json` (the suite had no standalone runner).

### Notes
- AC1's "one ack comment" is implemented as one ack reply per resolved thread (the capability surface's per-thread ack reply) — each closed conversation carries its own why.
- gh-807's withheld-arm decision unchanged (non-goal); mergeBot needs no change — it merges once GitHub recomputes `mergeable_state` to CLEAN after resolution.
- AC4 (live) verifies on the next approved-with-suggestions PR; the leg is idempotent, so ticks before that are harmless no-ops.

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.

## References

- gh-807 rules; #683/#710/#744 (thread/rework ownership family).
- Operator note: the 2026-10-10 fleet threads were resolved by hand (owner-approved one-off); this card makes that the machine's job.

## Summary

Solid, well-tested fix for the real 8h BLOCKED fleet stall: pure selection helpers with fail-closed gates, provider primitives with fail-open reads, per-thread failure isolation, and genuinely good test coverage (AC1 replay, AC2/AC3, fail-closed paths, idempotency, gitlab no-op). ## Key Issues

- ⚠️ **`threadSeverity` word-regex matches "non-blocking"** — `\bBLOCKING\b` matches the tail of "non-blocking"/"unblocking", so a machine suggestion comment containing that phrase is classified `blocking`, never auto-resolved, and can re-strand the PR BLOCKED (reviewVerdicts.js:380).

Pre-existing reader gap, but this PR's gate is its highest-stakes consumer.
- 💡 Ack reply is not idempotent: if `resolveThread` fails after the ack posted, the next tick posts another ack to the same thread (machineSmAgent.js:279).
- 💡 `maxResolveThreads` ignores the project-config `machineSm` override priority every other knob honors (machineSmAgent.js:325).

## Next Steps

1. Fix the severity regex (emoji-first, or a `(?:^|[^\w-])` guard before the word `BLOCKING`).
2. Thread the gh-728 machine-author allowlist into `verdictRecords` / `readVerdictRecords` (or document the accepted forge risk explicitly).
3. Optional: swap resolve-then-reply or dedupe acks on re-tick; honor `override.maxResolveThreads`.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `\bBLOCKING\b` matches "non-blocking" — suggestion threads can be misclassified and re-strand the PR**

`SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|(\bBLOCKING\b)/i` — the `\b` boundary holds across a hyphen, so any machine comment containing "non-blocking" / "unblocking" (very plausible in a reviewer's own suggestion prose, e.g. *"this is non-blocking, but consider renaming"*) classifies as `blocking`. Consequences:

- The thread is excluded from auto-resolution and keeps the rework arm — fine in isolation.
- But on an APPROVE + `blocking=0` head the rework arm is withheld (gh-828's own premise), so this thread is now owned by **nobody**: the new leg skips it, the rework arm never fires, and the conversation gate holds the PR BLOCKED — a permanent, per-thread recurrence of the exact 8h stall this PR fixes. Verified: `/\bBLOCKING\b/i.test('this is non-blocking, but consider renaming')` → `true`.

Fail-closed direction is right (a misclassified thread is never *wrongly resolved*), so this is not a merge blocker — but the classifier should match the marker convention precisely. Suggested fix: check the emoji markers first and require the word form to not follow a hyphen/word char:

```javascript
var SEVERITY_BLOCKING_RE = /(\uD83D\uDEA8)|((?:^|[^\w-])BLOCKING\b)/i;
```

A test with body `'💡 SUGGESTION: this is non-blocking, but rename'` → `'suggestion'` would pin it.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the ack reply is not idempotent — a persistent resolve failure spams one ack per tick**

The selection filters *resolved* threads, but the ack reply is posted **before** the resolve. If `replyToThread` succeeds and `resolveThread` throws (transient GraphQL error, token permission drift), the thread stays unresolved; next tick it is selected again and another ack is posted — one duplicate ack per tick per thread, unbounded, until the resolve starts succeeding (or forever, if the failure is persistent and the reply keeps working).

Cheapest fix: resolve first, then reply only when the resolve succeeded (a resolved thread missing its ack is a cosmetic loss; the code already tolerates `replyToThread` failing after a successful resolve — the information value of the ack is identical either way). Alternatively keep the order but track per-thread "ack already posted" — though no cross-tick state exists today.

Not blocking: requires resolve to keep failing while reply keeps succeeding, and the PR-level fallback path in `replyToThread` makes duplicate acks visible rather than destructive.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `maxResolveThreads` bypasses the documented override priority**

Every other `machineSm` knob resolves `override` (`.dmtools/config.js` `machineSm` section) before `p` (jobParams): `dryRun`, `maxConcurrentRuns`, `maxReworkRounds`, `workflowFile`, `issueLimit`… `maxResolveThreads` reads only `p.maxResolveThreads`, so a project that configures `machineSm: { maxResolveThreads: 5 }` in `.dmtools/config.js` gets the default 20 with no warning — surprising for an operator tuning the exact API-call bound this knob exists to control. One-liner for parity:

```javascript
cfg.maxResolveThreads = (typeof override.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && override.maxResolveThreads > 0)
    ? Math.floor(override.maxResolveThreads)
    : (typeof p.maxResolveThreads === 'number' && p.maxResolveThreads > 0)
        ? Math.floor(p.maxResolveThreads) : reviewVerdictsModule.DEFAULT_RESOLVE_THREADS_CAP;
```

# gh-828: [GOAL] Post-APPROVE suggestion threads never resolve — machine must resolve non-blocking threads (verdict blocking=0) in-tick; BLOCKED fleet stall 8h (fa #1457-#1470)

## Description

## Goal

A machine-approved PR (sticky `pr_approved`, verdict APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings) whose remaining review threads are non-blocking suggestions must get those threads RESOLVED by the machine in the same tick — an unresolved-thread conversation gate blocks the merge forever and no leg owns them.

## Subject

Tick arming-side action (gh-807, `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` consumers) + the merge gate. Live incident 2026-10-10 ~05:5xZ: fa PRs #1457/#1458/#1461/#1462/#1465/#1468/#1470 — all `pr_approved + ai_pr_reviewed + ai_validated`, ALL `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` (4-13 unresolved threads each), zero merges for ~8h. gh-807 correctly WITHHELD the rework arm (APPROVE + blocking=0 → "suggestions do not trigger rework") — but the rework leg is the ONLY owner of thread resolution, so the suggestion threads stayed open and the conversation gate held every head BLOCKED indefinitely.

## Capability surface

- New post-APPROVE action (or extension of the gh-807 withheld-arm branch): for each unresolved thread on an approved head, check the machine verdict record — blocking==0 for that thread's findings ⇒ post a short ack reply ("non-blocking suggestion — resolved per APPROVE verdict") and `resolveReviewThread`.
- Threads with blocking>0 never resolve here (they keep the rework arm).
- Only machine-authored threads resolve (never human threads; human-authored unresolved threads keep BLOCKED and surface to humans, same philosophy as gh-744 never-resolve-humans).
- Idempotent + bounded: limit ~20 threads/tick/card; already-resolved skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim — approved head with 4 suggestion threads ⇒ after one tick all 4 resolved + one ack comment; mergeState leaves BLOCKED.
2. AC2: a thread whose findings include blocking>0 is NOT resolved and the rework arm stands.
3. AC3: human-authored threads never auto-resolved.
4. AC4: live — the next approved-with-suggestions PR merges within its normal window without manual thread resolution.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the per-thread blocking classification (verdict record mapping).
- L2: replay the #1457-#1470 timeline against the new action.
- L3 (live): next occurrence resolves in-tick; monitor verifies no 8h BLOCKED fleet recurs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-807 withheld-arm decision itself (APPROVE+0-blocking ⇒ no rework stays).
- Resolving threads pre-approval.
